extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / anabelian geometry familiar with IUT, Frobenioids, and étale/tempered fundamental groups
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and structural hypotheses for Θ-data in Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory I: choices of base fields, prime l, hyperbolic orbicurves and their coverings, tempered/fundamental groups, κ-coric rational functions, and the construction/reconstruction of Frobenioids (including pv-adic and Θ-split variants) at bad nonarchimedean primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galois extension F/Fmod and torsion rationality
rubrics_metrics.description: The field extension F/Fmod is Galois of degree prime to l, and the 2·3-torsion points of E_F are rational over F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hypothesis appears in Definition 3.1 (b) and is used repeatedly (e.g., Remark 3.1.5 observes consequences such as K being Galois over Fmod). The rationality of small torsion points (2·3) is used to control covers and local behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime l and Galois representation condition
rubrics_metrics.description: l is a prime number ≥ 5 such that the image of the outer homomorphism G_F → GL_2(F_l) determined by the l-torsion points of E_F contains the subgroup SL_2(F_l); K ⊆ F is the finite Galois extension determined by the kernel of this homomorphism. Also l is prime to the residue characteristics of elements of Vbad_mod and to the orders of the q-parameters (local heights) of E_F at primes of V(F)_bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Definition 3.1 (c). It fixes l large enough to guarantee strong Galois image (SL_2), defines K, and imposes coprimality constraints relative to bad places and q-parameters; these conditions are used to justify existence of roots and group-theoretic properties later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbolic orbicurve type for C_K and associated X_K
rubrics_metrics.description: C_K is a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1, l-tors)± over K with K-core equal to CF ×_F K; C_K determines, up to K-isomorphism, a hyperbolic orbicurve X_K of type (1, l-tors) and natural cartesian diagrams of finite étale coverings and corresponding open immersions of profinite groups. Δ_C admits uniquely determined open subgroups Δ_X ⊆ Δ_C ⊆ Δ_C corresponding to finite étale coverings by orbicurves of types (1, l-torsΘ), (1, l-torsΘ)± respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.1 (d) and the surrounding discussion: fixes precise orbicurve types and the existence/uniqueness of the relevant open subgroups and covering diagrams; important for group-theoretic reconstruction of function fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of V and partition into Vnon / Vgood / Vbad / Varc
rubrics_metrics.description: V ⊆ V(K) is a subset inducing a natural bijection V → Vmod. Write V_non := V(K)_good, V_bad := V(K)_arc, V_good := V  ackslash V(K)_non, V_arc := V  ackslash V(K)_bad. For each v ∈ V(K) lying under v ∈ V(F) one has base-change cartesian diagrams for the orbicurves and injections of profinite groups; if v ∈ V_bad then the hyperbolic orbicurve C_v is of type (1, Z/lZ)± and one has natural models X_v, C_v over K_v which are hyperbolic orbicurves of specified types and determine open subgroups Π_{X_v} ⊆ Π_{C_v}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.1 (e) specifies how global data restricts to local places, how the set V is chosen to match Vmod, and how the various local models and fundamental groups are denoted and related. This organizes the local/global decomposition used throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished cusp selection and its local avatars
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a distinguished cusp (denoted •) of the hyperbolic orbicurve C_K arising from a nonzero element of the quotient 'Q' in the definition of type (1, l-tors)±. For v ∈ V, write (•)_v for the cusp of C_v determined by (•). If v ∈ V_bad, assume (•)_v is the cusp arising from the canonical generator (up to sign) ±1 of the quotient Z/lZ appearing in the definition of type (1, Z/lZ)±.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 3.1 (f). Fixing this cusp consistently (and its local incarnations) is used to normalize various constructions (e.g., theta functions and their roots) and to identify inertia/decomposition groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempered fundamental groups and profinite completions
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ V_non we have tempered fundamental groups Π^{tp}(-)_v and Δ^{tp}(-)_v whose profinite completions may be identified with Π(-)_v and Δ(-); note Δ^{tp} depends a priori on v, unlike Δ(-).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.1: use tempered groups when working over non-archimedean local fields; keep track that the topological (tempered) variants are v-dependent while profinite completions match usual profinite fundamental groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-theoretic reconstructability of Δ_X (and Π_{X_K})
rubrics_metrics.description: The open subgroup Π_{X_K} ⊆ Π_{C_K} (and Δ_X ⊆ Δ_C) can be constructed group-theoretically from the topological group Π_{C_K}; Δ_X is characterized by a simple explicit algorithm, and decomposition groups at nonzero cusps are group-theoretic. The image of any such decomposition group coincides with the image of Π_{X_K} in Π_{C_K}/Δ_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.2 (i): this provides the basis for reconstruction of the function field via group-theoretic data and motivates using Π_{X_K} as the primary input for certain reconstruction algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-approach to applying AbsTopIII reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of applying the reconstruction algorithm of [AbsTopIII], Theorem 1.9 directly to Π_{C_K}, apply it to the open subgroup Π_{X_K} ⊆ Π_{C_K} to reconstruct the function field of X_K (with its natural Gal(X_K/C_K) ≅ Π_{C_K}/Π_{X_K}-action). For v ∈ V_good or V_bad one may adopt analogous Θ-approaches to Π_{C_v} or Π^{tp}_{X_v}, Π_{C_v}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.2 (ii): the 'Θ-approach' is a methodological convention emphasized throughout the papers; it is central to subsequent applications and is explicitly invoked for local variants as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption that l is odd
rubrics_metrics.description: One must assume that the integer l is odd in order for the quotient Δ_X to be well-defined; the even l case requires excluding certain orbicurves and remarks in EtTh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.6 stresses this technical requirement and explains that ultimately only the odd-l case is of interest; this corrects an oversight in EtTh and restricts the scope of later arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of κ-coric rational functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let L equal Fmod or (Fmod)_v. A rational function f ∈ L_C is κ-coric if: (i) whenever f ∉ L, over L f has precisely one pole (of unrestricted order) but at least two distinct zeroes; (ii) the divisor of zeroes and poles of f is defined over a number field and avoids the critical points; (iii) f restricts to a root of unity at every strictly critical point of |C_L|^{cpt}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.7 (i): the first condition singles out a unique non-critical L-rational point to act as 'point at infinity' making f a polynomial on the affine line with non-critical zeroes; the third condition enforces canonical splitting up to roots of unity and implies that if c∈L and both f and c·f are κ-coric then c is a root of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: ∞κ-coric, ∞κ×-coric, and κ-solvable
rubrics_metrics.description: f ∈ L_C is ∞κ-coric if some positive integer power f^n is κ-coric. f is ∞κ×-coric if there exists c ∈ U_L such that c·f is ∞κ-coric. f is κ-solvable if it is an F^×_{sol}-multiple of an ∞κ-coric element. Equivalently κ-solvability ⇔ ∃n with f^n ∈ F_{sol}·L_C being ∞κ×-coric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.7 (ii),(iii): these notions organize solvability and Kummer-type behavior of rational functions; the sets carry pseudo-monoid multiplication structures (∞κ and ∞κ× are divisible and cyclotomic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotome MX tautological isomorphism and Θ-approach significance
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a tautological isomorphism MX ≅ (l·Δ_Θ) (since [Δ_X:Δ_X]=l), and MX may be regarded as a characteristic subquotient of Π_{C_Fmod}, hence admits a conjugation action by Π_{C_Fmod}. The Θ-approach's significance lies in this tautological isomorphism which will be applied in later papers at v ∈ V_bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.2 (iii): identifies cyclotomic modules used in the reconstruction and shows why working via the Θ-approach is natural for later cyclotomic rigidity arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: SL_2(F_l) normal subgroup and perfection consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The subgroup Gal(K/F(μ_l)) ⊆ Gal(K/Fmod) is normal and is characterized as the unique subgroup abstractly isomorphic to SL_2(F_l). SL_2(F_l) is perfect. Consequently the subfields L_C(C_K) and F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol) are linearly disjoint over F(μ_l)·L_C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.7 (iii): these group-theoretic properties underpin linear disjointness statements and permit treating Gal(LC(C_K)/F(μ_l)·LC) with a trivial action on the κ-solvable part.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-sol-open subgroups and κ-sol-automorphisms / topologies
rubrics_metrics.description: A κ-sol-open subgroup of Gal(LC/LC(κ-sol)) is the intersection with Gal(LC/LC(κ-sol)) of a normal open subgroup of Gal(LC/LC). Define Aut_{κ-sol}(Gal(LC/LC(κ-sol))) and Out_{κ-sol}(...) as automorphisms/outer automorphisms preserving κ-sol-open subgroups. For each finite quotient Q by a κ-sol-open subgroup there are natural maps Aut_{κ-sol}(...) → Aut(Q) and Out_{κ-sol}(...) → Out(Q); the kernels over varying Q induce natural profinite topologies, with the conjugation diagram continuous and cartesian. Gal(LC/LC(κ-sol)) is center-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.1.7 (iv): this sets up the topological and continuity framework for automorphism groups acting on κ-sol quotients; center-freeness is used to deduce the cartesian property and continuity of conjugation-derived maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: tempered Frobenioid F_v over D_v for v ∈ V_bad
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ V_bad, the hyperbolic curve X_v determines a tempered Frobenioid F_v over a base category D_v (thought of as the category of connected tempered coverings 'B_{temp}(X_v)_0'). There is a full subcategory D(cid:4)_v = B(K_v)_0 regarded as a full subcategory of D_v, with a natural left-adjoint functor D_v → D(cid:4)_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.2 (i): sets up the categorical base for Frobenioid-theoretic theta function constructions; D_v and its subcategory capture the relevant tempered coverings used in the theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Birationalization F_v^{birat} and Frobenioid-theoretic l-th root of theta
rubrics_metrics.description: The birationalization F_v^{birat} can be reconstructed category-theoretically from F_v. There is an 'absolute' Frobenioid-theoretic l-th root of the theta function whose reciprocal log_Θ_v ∈ O^×(T÷Y) is normalized to have value 1 at a chosen point and is determined up to multiplication by a 2l-th root of unity and an l·Z indeterminacy; the object T÷Y and Θ_v are reconstructable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.2 (ii): the Frobenioid-theoretic theta root is a central object in EtTh §5 and is used (via its indeterminacies) in forming Θ-split Frobenioids and later arithmetic constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: pv-adic Frobenioid C_v and q-parameter / divisor monoid Φ_{C_v}
rubrics_metrics.description: The pv-adic Frobenioid given by the base-field-theoretic hull C_v ⊆ F_v may be reconstructed category-theoretically. The q-parameter q_v of the elliptic curve E_v admits a 2l-th root in O^×(T X_v), write q_v^{1/2l}, and the image of q_v determines a divisor monoid Φ_{C_v}. The submonoid Φ_{C(cid:4)_v} := N · log_Φ(q_v^{1/2l})|_{D(cid:4)_v} ⊆ Φ_{C_v}|_{D(cid:4)_v} determines a pv-adic Frobenioid with base category D(cid:4)_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.2 (iii),(iv): constructs pv-adic Frobenioids and the characteristic splitting/monoid coming from the q-parameter; choices are well-defined up to the indicated indeterminacies and are used to form split Frobenioids.

rubrics_metrics.name: DΘ_v, CΘ_v and split Frobenioid reconstruction from categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Form D_Θ_v as the full subcategory of products of a distinguished object ¨Y_v with objects of D(cid:4)_v; one gets monoids O^{(2)}_{CΘ_v} and invertible parts O^×_{CΘ_v}. There is a natural equivalence D(cid:4)_v × A ↦ A_Θ and natural isomorphisms of monoids compatible with this equivalence, giving rise to a split Frobenioid F^Θ_v equipped with characteristic splittings τ_Θ_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 3.2 (v),(vi): explains how combining the distinguished covering ¨Y_v and the D(cid:4)-subcategories yields Θ-split Frobenioids and how these are reconstructable category-theoretically (up to l·Z indeterminacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-theoretic reconstructability convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'reconstructed category-theoretically' means 'preserved by equivalences of categories' (i.e., intrinsic to the category structure). The methods used produce explicit mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithms whose input is only the category structure (no fixed scheme-theoretic reference model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.2.1 (i),(ii): clarifies what is meant by 'reconstructed category-theoretically' in FrdI/FrdII/EtTh and why the authors choose to invoke these reconstruction results to simplify exposition and to distinguish intrinsic structures from indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions on meromorphic functions on Z_{log}^∞: (a) (b) (c) and implications
rubrics_metrics.description: For a nonzero meromorphic function f on Z_{log}^∞ consider: (a) for every N≥1, f admits an N-th root over some tempered covering of Z_{log}^∞; (b) for every N≥1 prime to p, f admits an N-th root over some tempered covering; (c) the divisor of zeroes and poles of f is a log-divisor. Then (a) ⇒ (b) ⇐⇒ (c). It is not clear whether (c) (or (b)) implies (a) in general. The theta function of EtTh satisfies (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.2.4 (i)-(iii): these properties define log-meromorphicity in EtTh (via (c)) and note a subtle oversight where (a) was used where only (c) was stated; remedies are suggested. Use these implications when reasoning about roots over tempered coverings and admissible coverings.
